plainTranslation:
This person may unsettle you in small ways that are hard to explain. It might be how they handle silence, how quickly they need reassurance, how they pull back when something is wrong, or how they expect you to respond when they are upset. Their emotional style can press on yours.

When this works, it can make you more honest about your own patterns. You may start to notice what you do when you feel hurt, ignored, overwhelmed, or unsure. This person may not always make you comfortable, but they can show you where you get reactive, where you shut down, or where you expect someone else to know what you have not said.

The lesson is learning the difference between what happened and what it touched in you. Sometimes the other person really did miss you. Sometimes they only moved differently than you would have. Sometimes their mood is not about you, even if your body reacts like it is.

The harder part is that moods can start setting each other off. One person gets quiet and the other reads it as rejection. One person asks for closeness and the other feels crowded. One person tries to move on and the other feels dismissed. Suddenly the issue is not just what happened, but how both people felt about how it was handled.

Because this is emotional, it may not always make sense on paper. You can explain the facts perfectly and still feel bruised. That is what makes this contact tricky. The feelings are not always logical, but they are still real.

Pause before you turn the mood into a story. Ask what is actually needed. This connection gets easier when both people stop treating sensitivity as an accusation.
